I have $522 and four properties. p1 has $257 and a massive empire with 4 houses on monopolies. p2 and p4 are bankrupt.

I will keep my cash as a survival cushion and avoid trading Kentucky Avenue to p1. I am now calculating which spaces I can land on from Illinois Avenue.

I mapped the full board. From Illinois, a roll of 2 lands on B&O Railroad, which is unowned and could be purchased. A roll of 3 lands on Atlantic Avenue, mortgaged by p1.

Rolls 4 through 6 hit mortgaged properties. Rolls 7 through 12 hit p1's monopolies with four houses: Pacific, NC, and Pennsylvania. I am calculating the exact rent costs for these spaces.

Pennsylvania with four houses costs $1200. Pacific and NC cost $1100. I have $522 cash. I can mortgage Electric Company for $75, Kentucky Avenue for $110, and Boardwalk for $200.

Mortgaging all four properties yields only $907 total cash. That is still below the $1100–$1200 rent on p1’s green monopolies, so landing there would bankrupt me. The probability of hitting a green with four houses from Illinois is roughly 28%. B&O Railroad is unowned and could be purchased for $200, leaving about $322.

Unmortgaging Park Place would cost about $193, leaving only $329 cash. Without any houses in the bank, I cannot build anything. Even with a monopoly on Boardwalk, rent is just $100, which p1 can easily afford. Unmortgaging is not worth it.

I am now considering a trade with p1. I hold Electric Company, which would complete their utility monopoly if they acquire it. I also hold Kentucky Avenue, which blocks the reds and would prevent them from completing that set.

The dark blue monopoly is incomplete because Park Place is mortgaged. p1 is also on Illinois Avenue with $257, so they must roll and travel to reach my dark blues. I am weighing whether I can bankrupt them before they land on my properties.

The bank has no houses left. p1 owns all 32 houses and cannot build more until someone sells. I am now considering trading Kentucky Avenue plus cash for something useful.

I cannot survive the greens without more cash or a property that kills p1 before I die. p1 will not demolish houses for my benefit. No trade can save me from the board's four-house monopolies. I am likely to go bankrupt soon.

p1’s next roll from Illinois could land on B&O Railroad, which is unowned and worth $200. They have $257, so they might buy it. Rolls 3 through 6 would hit their own mortgaged yellows, where no rent is paid. A roll of 7 lands them in jail.

p1’s next roll from Illinois is safe. Their greens are not dangerous, and they would not pay rent to themselves. The nearest property on the forward path is Electric Company at space 12. Kentucky Avenue sits 37 spaces ahead, so it is unreachable this turn.

I am now calculating the exact distances from Illinois Avenue. Electric Company is 28 spaces away, so it is unreachable this turn. Park Place is 13 spaces ahead and Boardwalk is 15, meaning p1 cannot land on my dark blues for at least two turns.

My own roll next will have roughly a 28% chance of hitting greens and bankrupting me immediately. Even if I survive that roll, the board remains a minefield of p1's four-house monopolies.

I can survive the orange and brown monopolies with four houses, but the greens are fatal. The only way to win is to bankrupt p1 before I land on a green. Boardwalk without a monopoly costs only $50, so it cannot kill them.

Boardwalk rent is only $100 even with a dark-blue monopoly, so it cannot bankrupt p1. I have no houses to build, and p1 will not sell them unless they are desperate for cash. My low rents do not force that desperation, creating a chicken-and-egg problem.

I am now analyzing what p1 wants to trade. They need cash, a completed utility set, and a red monopoly. I have no properties that would give them those things. I cannot request that they sell houses in a trade. The available trades are unhelpful.

I am checking whether the game allows trading properties that already have houses. In standard Monopoly, buildings must be sold before a property can be traded, so p1's developed monopolies likely cannot be acquired directly. I am now looking at undeveloped properties they own as possible trade targets.

I checked every undeveloped property p1 owns. The light blues are all mortgaged, so they would yield no rent. The pinks are incomplete because Virginia is unowned. The reds are already split between us. None of these sets can kill p1 quickly.

I cannot complete a red monopoly because Indiana is mortgaged and I have no houses to build. The yellows are all mortgaged, so acquiring them would cost too much to unmortgage. Utilities and three railroads are not lethal. I am now checking whether I can trade anything of value with p1.

I cannot trade for houses. I am now looking for a deal p1 would accept that actually hurts them, since they want me bankrupt.

I am now weighing whether to trade Kentucky Avenue to p1. They could then complete a red monopoly, but unimproved reds only cost about $36–$40 in rent, which is harmless to me. The danger would only arise if they later build houses on those properties. I am also calculating whether p1 could free up houses by building hotels on their orange monopolies.

I realized that building a hotel returns the four houses to the bank. p1 has twelve hotels available, so they could reallocate houses by hoteling their orange, green, and brown properties. Hotel costs match house costs for each color group.

I realized that if p1 hotels their orange monopolies, the returned houses could let me build on my dark blues. However, I need an unmortgaged Park Place to start building, and doing so costs about $193. Even with $522 cash, I cannot afford both unmortgaging and building evenly on Boardwalk and Park Place. Mortgaging Electric Company and Kentucky Avenue would only raise my cash to $707, which is still insufficient.

I calculated the exact cash needed to build evenly on my dark blues. Unmortgaging Park Place costs $193, leaving $514. One house on each property costs $400, leaving $114. That is not enough for two houses on Boardwalk, which would cost another $400. Three houses on Boardwalk would require five total houses and roughly $1000, which I cannot afford. Two houses on each property would cost about $993.

Even the best possible build leaves me cash-broke. One house on each dark blue would cost $593, leaving only $114. Boardwalk with one house pays $200 and Park Place with one pays $175, but p1 would still have $57 and $82 left. I cannot bankrupt them that way, and any rent I owe would immediately bankrupt me.

Two houses on Boardwalk would pay $600, which exceeds p1’s $257. That would kill them, but building requires $793 total: $600 for the houses and $193 to unmortgage Park Place. With only $707 available, I am $86 short. I must unmortgage to build, so this path is impossible.

I considered selling Electric Company to p1 for cash. Even with $250, the math still leaves them nearly broke before they land on me.

I considered selling Electric Company for $100 instead of $250. That would raise my cash to about $732, but I still need roughly $600 to build evenly on Boardwalk and Park Place after unmortgaging. I remain $61 short, so this path does not solve the problem.

I calculated that selling Electric Company for $175 would leave me with exactly enough cash to build two houses on Boardwalk and one on Park Place. However, the bank currently holds zero houses, so I cannot construct anything until p1 sells or hotels their properties first. This creates a deadlock: I need cash now, but I cannot spend it until houses are returned.

I decided to end the turn and keep my cash liquid. Unmortgaging would waste $193, and mortgaging or trading would leave me without a cushion. I will wait until houses are actually available before spending any money.

I considered several trade offers, but none are viable. A deal that looks appealing to a human player would be mechanically harmful, and the AI evaluates trades rationally so it would reject any bad offer. Selling Boardwalk would destroy my only win condition, and giving up Park Place would lose my dark-blue monopoly.
